name: dock-magnify
summary: A macOS-style dock: each icon's size is a clamped linear function of its distance from the pointer along x, from 40px at rest to 60px under the cursor within 140px, settled on a spring rather than snapped.

size.description: Resting icon size in pixels. Upstream's DEFAULT_SIZE. Set --fx-dock-size to match so the no-script bar agrees.

magnification.description: Size in pixels of the icon directly under the pointer. Upstream's DEFAULT_MAGNIFICATION.

distance.description: How far along x the pointer's influence reaches, in pixels. Upstream's DEFAULT_DISTANCE.

deviations.what: React, framer-motion and class-variance-authority are all gone: useMotionValue / useTransform / useSpring become one anime createAnimatable per icon with a spring ease driven from a pointermove listener, and the two Tailwind class strings become the rules in style.css.
deviations.why: This library ships vanilla ES modules into generated sites with no build step, so a component is not a shippable unit. Every number survives the move -- size 40, magnification 60, distance 140, padding max(6, size * 0.2), and mass 0.1 / stiffness 150 / damping 12, which anime's spring takes under the same three names. The useTransform mapping is a clamped linear ramp between two points and is written out as one. marquee-css and cursor-spotlight are the same kind of port in this repo already.

deviations.what: The pointer is read from e.clientX rather than e.pageX.
deviations.why: Upstream compares e.pageX against getBoundingClientRect().x, and those two are in different coordinate systems -- they differ by the horizontal scroll offset. It never shows on the docs page, which does not scroll sideways, but a dock inside a horizontally scrolled region would magnify the wrong icon. clientX is the space the rect is already in.

deviations.what: pointermove and pointerleave listen on the bar rather than being props on the component, and the icons are looked up inside the section.
deviations.why: React passes mouseX down by cloning children; a vanilla mount has the DOM instead. Scoping both to this mount's own bar is what lets two docks sit on one page without each one driving the other.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion no listeners are attached and the icons stay at their resting size.
deviations.why: Effect contract: mount() stays at rest. Nothing is lost -- that is upstream's own disableMagnification mode, and the bar is still a complete row of working links rather than a control that has stopped doing its job.

deviations.what: Each icon carries a text label that appears on hover and on keyboard focus, and the section supplies six plain inline SVG glyphs.
deviations.why: Upstream's docs preview hands the component lucide icons from the page, so nothing about labelling is part of the component -- but a dock of unlabelled pictures is unreadable, and a keyboard user gets no hover at all. The glyphs are drawn here rather than pulled from an icon set so the effect ships no third-party art and a site can swap them for its own.
